name: Polynucleotide eye treatment (Plenhyl, Rejuran Healer)
lead: Polynucleotide (PN) eye treatment is a skin-booster procedure in which a clinician places tiny injections of purified DNA fragments, usually derived from salmon or trout, into the thin skin under the eyes. People use it to improve skin thickness, hydration and texture, with dark circles and crepey skin as the main targets, without adding the volume of a filler.[1][2]

Rejuran, made by PharmaResearch in South Korea, is the best-known brand; Plinest (Mastelli, Italy) is another.[1] Rejuran I is sold for the under-eye area and Rejuran Healer for the face, according to clinic sources.[2]

Fish-derived polynucleotide is described as used in aesthetic medicine as a dermal filler.[3] Providers describe clinical data showing gains in skin thickness, elasticity and hydration, though the clinic source cites no specific studies.[1]

chain: Micro-injections of polynucleotides placed in thin eye-area skin
Fibroblasts and hydration are reported to improve
angle.text: Clients seek it for thin, crepey under-eye skin and dark circles. Providers describe it as improving skin quality without adding volume.

paras: Polynucleotides and PDRN are purified DNA fragments prepared by repeated filtration to remove cellular material, proteins and potential allergens, leaving a sterile injectable.[1] Providers say they activate fibroblasts, support collagen and elastin, attract water, calm inflammation and aid barrier repair.[1]
Under-eye versions are described as having a thinner consistency suited to the delicate area, and are given by micro-injection after numbing cream.[2]

No studies found in the sources reviewed for this article that test under-eye polynucleotide injections. Providers state that clinical data on Rejuran and Plinest show gains in skin thickness, elasticity and hydration in other areas, without naming the papers.[1]

Appointments take about 30 minutes.[2] Providers describe glow improving within one to two weeks and deeper changes over four to eight weeks.[1] Small bumps at injection sites last 24 to 48 hours, a little longer under the eyes.[1]

Common effects are redness, swelling, bumps and mild discomfort that resolve within days.[1][2] Bruising is common in the eye area, and fish or salmon allergy is a stated contraindication in manufacturer-style guidance.
Social media popularised the "salmon DNA facial" label, which one clinician calls sensationalised.[1]

card.summary: Micro-injections of salmon-derived polynucleotides under the eyes to thicken and smooth thin, crepey skin and soften dark circles.
card.aka: Rejuran I, Rejuran Healer, PN skin booster, salmon DNA facial
card.note: Contraindicated with fish allergy; not approved as an injectable in the US.

quick.overview:
A clinician injects purified polynucleotides, usually from salmon, into the skin under the eyes. It is sought for thin, crepey skin and dark circles.

Providers describe it as improving skin thickness and hydration without adding volume. A course is usually three to four sessions.
quick.mechanism: Polynucleotides are said to stimulate fibroblasts for collagen and elastin, attract water and support the skin barrier. Glow may appear within weeks, deeper changes by four to eight weeks.
quick.risks: Redness, swelling, bumps and bruising are common and resolve in days. Fish allergy is a contraindication. No injectable polynucleotide is FDA-approved, and efficacy claims mostly come from providers.
